title: interactive: surface mutagen sync conflicts instead of silent freeze
description:
## Problem

Live HPC session confirmed: mutagen two-way-safe sessions accumulate conflicts across jernerics session churn (every terminate+create wipes the baseline; any file differing across endpoints at recreation becomes a permanent '<non-existent> -> File' conflict). Conflicted files propagate in neither direction. Both is_converged() and the reconnect check in _ensure_interactive_sync ignore the conflict count, so the CLI reports sync as live/running while files are frozen.

## Locked design (user-approved)

Surface-only, never overwrite:
- Parse {{len .Conflicts}} into SessionInfo; is_converged requires conflicts == 0; is_idle keeps the old Watching+connected semantics and gates start() (must NOT trigger the tar/scp one-shot fallback on conflicts).
- Reconnect path: 'already running' only when healthy; otherwise print status/connected/conflicts + conflicted paths + remediation, no restart.
- Fresh path: warn + list paths after start when conflicts > 0.
- conflicted_paths(name) via dedicated sync list template.
- Add .direnv/ to INTERACTIVE_EXCLUDES (absolute nix-store symlinks cause scan problems).
close_reason: Completed: conflict-aware SessionInfo/is_converged/is_idle split, conflicted_paths(), report-only _warn_sync_unhealthy in reconnect+fresh paths, .direnv/ excluded. Verified: 122 tests, just lint, just format-check exit 0; live daemon probe parses conflicts=0, is_converged=True; production reconnect path prints 'already running' against real session.

title: Container build provides no progress feedback during jernerics run
description:
## Problem

During `jernerics run`, the container build step (Apptainer/Docker) can take 10-20 minutes. There is no progress feedback — the command appears to hang. This is especially bad for agents that need to decide whether to keep waiting or investigate.

## What happens

```
$ jernerics run trial.py config.py --backend hpc
Syncing project...
Building container...   # <- hangs here for 10-20 min with no output
Submitting job...
```

The Apptainer build runs over SSH and its output isn't streamed back.

## Proposed solution

Stream the container build output (or at least progress milestones) back to the caller. Options:

1. Stream SSH stdout/stderr line-by-line during build
2. Print periodic status: "Building container... (3/8 steps)" 
3. Add a `--verbose` flag that enables full output streaming

Even knowing "the build is at step 3 of 8" would prevent agents and humans from thinking the process is hung.
close_reason: Implemented in commit bf10602

title: Cancelled jobs leave orphan checker dependencies pending
description:
## Problem
When `jernerics cancel -b hpc <job_id>` cancels a SLURM job, it cancels the
main array job but leaves the checker dependency job (submitted with
`--dependency=afterany:$ARRAY_JOB_ID`) in PENDING state forever.

## Evidence
On 2026-08-06, ~12 orphan checker jobs accumulated as PENDING with reason
`QOSMinGRES` after multiple experiment cancellations. Each jernerics run
submits two jobs: the array job + a checker job with `--dependency=afterany`.
Cancelling via `jernerics cancel` only kills the array job.

## Fix
`jernerics cancel` should cancel the entire job chain — both the array job
and any checker/dependency jobs associated with it. Options:
1. Track both job IDs at submission time and cancel both
2. Look up dependent jobs via `squeue --dependency` and cancel them
3. Cancel by job name pattern (the checker jobs share the study name)

## Location
The cancel command is in `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/cli.py`.
The job submission (array + checker) is in
`packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/adapter.py`.
close_reason: Completed: commit c56d699. cancel() now finds and kills dependent checker jobs via squeue dependency lookup.

title: Script-as-trial: runner executes scripts via subprocess + remove old trial() function path
description:
## Scope

Replace the runner's trial execution model: instead of `from trial import trial; trial(config, tracker)`, the runner writes the resolved config to JSON, sets `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG`, and executes the script via subprocess.

## CRITICAL: No backward compatibility

Do NOT add backward compatibility. Do NOT add a fallback that tries `from trial import trial` first. Do NOT add deprecation warnings. The old entry point is gone — the ONLY execution path is subprocess execution of the script.

## Depends on

- `jernerics-rs5` (trial context API must exist first)

## Changes

### runner.py
- Before executing the trial, write the resolved config dict to a JSON file in the cache dir (e.g., `{cache_dir}/configs/trial_{config_index}.json`)
- Set `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var to point at this file
- Execute via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(trial_file)])` instead of importing and calling a function
- The trial file is the first positional argument to `jernerics run` (or `jernerics local`)
- Read trial results: the script calls `tracker.finish(results)` which writes to the tracker. The runner reads results from the tracker output (JSONL or whatever the tracker writes).

### Remove old path
- Remove the code path that does `from trial import trial; trial(config, tracker)`
- Remove any tests that mock `trial(config, tracker)` or test the function-call execution model
- Update ALL existing tests in the test suite that assume the function-call model

### CLI changes
- `jernerics run` and `jernerics local` already take a trial file as the first positional arg. This does not change.
- The trial file is now executed as a script, not imported

## Test updates

This is the high-effort part. All tests that currently:
- Mock `trial(config, tracker)` 
- Assert the runner calls a trial function
- Test config injection via function arguments

...must be rewritten to:
- Use subprocess execution model
- Assert env var is set
- Assert script is executed
- Mock or provide a simple trial script for E2E tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Runner writes resolved config JSON and sets env var
- [ ] Runner executes trial scripts via subprocess
- [ ] Old `from trial import trial` path completely removed
- [ ] All tests updated and passing
- [ ] No backward compatibility shims
close_reason: Completed: commit d5bb4e4. Runner executes trial scripts via subprocess, sets JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG env var. Old trial() function path removed. 643 tests pass.

title: Show study_name in jernerics jobs output (bridge job to tracking)
description:
## Problem

Job metadata (`save_job_meta`) does not store `study_name`. Without it, there is no bridge from a scheduler job to its tracking data. The overnight OMP run exposed this: the agent could see jobs were RUNNING but had to SSH and parse `.out` files to know what study or step they were at.

## Scope (revised after discussion with Jerry)

**Only add `study_name` to job meta + display it as a column in `jernerics jobs`.** Do NOT add metrics to jobs — that is `jernerics summary`'s job. Clean separation:

- `jernerics jobs` → scheduler view (job_id, study_name, status)
- `jernerics summary <study>` → metrics view (loss, step, params)

```
JOB_ID      STUDY                       STATUS
26887165    overfit_seed42              RUNNING
26887168    overfit_seed123             RUNNING
```

Then `jernerics summary overfit_seed42` takes you to the metrics.

## Implementation

1. `save_job_meta` — add `study_name` field at submission time
2. `cli.py::jobs()` — add STUDY column, read from job meta
3. Update `JobInfo` model if needed

## Test plan

- Unit: job meta includes study_name after submission
- Unit: jobs table renders study column
- Backward compat: old job meta without study_name shows blank

## Definition of done

1. `just check` passes
2. `just typecheck` passes
3. Commit: `feat(cli): show study_name in jobs output (jernerics-8g8)`

title: log_metric as documented alias for log_value
description: Spun off jernerics-df6 investigation. symlab's trial code called tracker.log_metric() against a protocol that only defines log_value/log_param/log_artifact/finish. Two options: (a) add log_metric as an alias in TrackerProtocol implementations (ConsoleTracker, _JobTracker) for discoverability, (b) improve docs. Alias is cheap and prevents a whole class of silent API mismatch bugs that only surface on HPC (container) runs.

title: Workspace path dependencies break container builds
description:
## Problem

When a project uses local path dependencies (e.g., symlab depends on jernerics via `../jernerics/packages/jernerics`), container builds fail because the path dependency doesn't exist inside the container build context.

## Reproduction

```toml
# symlab/pyproject.toml
[tool.uv.sources]
jernerics = { path = "../jernerics/packages/jernerics", editable = true }
```

The container.def copies project files and runs `uv sync`, but `../jernerics/` doesn't exist in the container. The build fails.

## Current workaround

Create a separate pyproject.toml for the container that replaces path deps with git deps:
```toml
[tool.uv.sources]
jernerics = { git = "https://github.com/...", subdirectory = "packages/jernerics" }
```

## Proposed solution

Options:
1. jernerics automatically detects path deps and warns/instructs before container build
2. A `jernerics containerize` command that generates a container-appropriate pyproject.toml from the project's config
3. Document this as a known limitation in the deployment guide with the workaround pattern
4. Support a `.containerignore` or `.container-pyproject.toml` overlay that jernerics uses during build
close_reason: Detection + fail-fast implemented in commit 3fe1925. Overlay system deferred until push-to-test round-trip becomes a real pain point.

title: _JobTracker API mismatch between local and container jernerics versions
description:
## Problem
The local jernerics has `trial_tracker()` returning a tracker with `log_metric()` and `log_param()` methods. The container's jernerics (installed in /opt/venv) returns a `_JobTracker` that does NOT have these methods.

## Error
```
AttributeError: '_JobTracker' object has no attribute 'log_metric'
```

This causes every trial to fail with exit code 1, even when the actual cell execution succeeds and records are saved correctly.

## Impact
All HPC runs report as 'failed' even when they succeed. Records are saved before the tracker crash, but optuna marks trials as failed.

## Repro
Any `jernerics run` with a trial file that calls `tracker.log_metric()` or `tracker.log_param()`.

## Workaround
None — the tracker API needs to be consistent between local and container versions.
close_reason: Symlab-side bug: code called nonexistent log_metric; fixed by switching to log_value in commit pending symlab side. jernerics behaved correctly.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Root cause found — NOT a version mismatch. Local and container jernerics are identical (git-pinned, same lockfile). The real bug: symlab's trial scripts called tracker.log_metric(), a method that has never existed in jernerics' TrackerProtocol (the API is log_param/log_value/log_artifact/finish). Fixed symlab-side in trial.py, pysips_paper_trial.py, runner.py. No jernerics change needed. However, a DX improvement remains valid: _JobTracker could expose log_metric as an alias, or the protocol docs could make the API more discoverable.

title: Container build marker doesn't hash container.def — stale builds
description:
## Problem

The container build marker (`needs_rebuild` / `write_marker`) doesn't hash the `container.def` file content. If you modify the container definition, `jernerics run` doesn't detect the change and skips the rebuild. You have to manually pass `--force`.

## Reproduction

1. `jernerics run` — builds container, writes marker
2. Edit `container.def`
3. `jernerics run` again — says container is up to date, skips build

## Fix

Include a hash of `container.def` (and `pyproject.toml` / `pyproject.container.toml` if used) in the build marker. On subsequent runs, compare the hash to detect changes.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8b436ab

title: Script-as-trial: replace trial function with plain Python script execution
description:
## Overview

Replace the `def trial(config, tracker)` function entry point with plain script execution. The same file runs standalone (prototyping) or via the runner (batch/SLURM) with zero modifications.

## API

```python
import jernerics

config = jernerics.trial_config(defaults={
    "lr": 3e-4, "n_steps": 100, "d_model": 128, ...
})

tracker = jernerics.trial_tracker()

model = build_model(config)
for step in range(config["n_steps"]):
    loss = train_step(model, config)
    tracker.log_value("loss", loss, step=step)

tracker.finish({"final_loss": loss})
```

Zero conditionals. Zero null checks. Works in both modes.

## Design

### trial_config(defaults: dict | None = None) -> dict
- **Job mode:** reads injected JSON from `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var
- **Standalone mode:** returns the `defaults` dict as-is
- Raises if job mode but env var not set
- Raises if standalone mode and no `defaults` provided

### trial_tracker() -> Tracker | ConsoleTracker
- **Job mode:** returns real `Tracker` (JSONL + server ship)
- **Standalone mode:** returns `ConsoleTracker` that prints to stdout
- Both implement same protocol: `log_param`, `log_value`, `finish`
- `ConsoleTracker.log_value` prints `[step N] key=value`
- `ConsoleTracker.finish` prints trial summary
- `ConsoleTracker.log_param` prints `param: key=value`

### is_job() -> bool
- Returns True if `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var is set (running as a scheduled job)
- Returns False when running standalone (python trial.py)
- Escape hatch for genuinely different behavior between modes

### tracker.finish(results: dict)
- **Tracker:** records results, picks up by runner as Optuna objective value
- **ConsoleTracker:** prints summary

## Runner changes

- `runner.py`: instead of `from trial import trial; trial(config, tracker)`, do:
  1. Write resolved config to temp JSON file
  2. Set `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var
  3. `subprocess.run(["python", trial_file])`
- Runner reads `tracker.finish()` results from the tracker output (or a known file)

## Breaking changes

- Drop `def trial(config, tracker)` entry point entirely (no backward compat)
- All symlab trial files need rewriting from function to script
- `load_config()` in config.py stays the same (still reads config.py files with base/grid/search_space)

## Trial protocol (type annotation)

```python
class TrackerProtocol(Protocol):
    def log_param(self, key: str, value: str) -> None: ...
    def log_value(self, key: str, value: float, step: int) -> None: ...
    def finish(self, results: dict[str, Any]) -> None: ...
```

## User Stories

1. **Prototype locally:** `python trial.py` runs with defaults config, prints metrics to console
2. **Submit to SLURM:** `jernerics run --backend hpc trial.py config.py` submits same file unchanged
3. **Grid sweep:** same file, runner materializes configs, each SLURM task gets its own env var
4. **Optuna search:** same file, runner asks study for suggestions, writes resolved config
5. **Marimo notebook as trial:** marimo .py files run via `python notebook.py` (marimo native script mode)
6. **Debug failed trial:** resolved configs written to cache for reproducibility
7. **Result feedback:** `tracker.finish()` → runner picks up → records in tracking / feeds Optuna objective

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `trial_config()`, `trial_tracker()`, `is_job()` implemented
- [ ] `ConsoleTracker` prints metrics to stdout
- [ ] Runner executes trial scripts via subprocess instead of function import
- [ ] All existing symlab trial files rewritten as scripts
- [ ] All jernerics tests pass
- [ ] `python trial.py` works standalone in symlab
- [ ] `jernerics run --backend hpc trial.py config.py` works end-to-end
close_reason: Split into three subtasks for incremental delivery

title: Restructure CLI and add safe interactive sync resolution
description:
Restructure the growing flat CLI into domain subcommands and add explicit, data-safe interactive sync inspection and conflict resolution.

Locked design:
- Keep root commands: init, local, run.
- Add groups: interactive start/stop/sync, job, backend, tracking.
- Clean cutover with no compatibility aliases.
- Split cli.py into a thin root plus jernerics.commands domain modules before changing behavior.
- Replace tracking sync + replay with tracking replay; no --backend uses local cache, --backend NAME replays from that backend.
- interactive sync status is report-only, supports JSON, and exits zero for successfully inspected missing/unhealthy states.
- Project-owned .jernericsignore uses Git-style patterns and applies with .gitignore plus shared defaults to deploy tar sync, interactive Mutagen, and one-shot fallback. Never silently restart sessions when ignore configuration changes.
- Resolver accepts explicit PATH... and --from local|cluster; no --all; regular files present on both endpoints only.
- Preview then confirm; --yes for noninteractive use and --dry-run for preview only.
- Back up every losing file locally under XDG_STATE_HOME (default ~/.local/state), with manifest and verified checksums, before any overwrite.
- Copy one path at a time via a checksum-verified destination temporary file and atomic replace. Stop on first failure, never auto-rollback, and report partial results.
- Recheck hashes for races, flush Mutagen, and require selected conflicts to disappear. Never restart or use one-shot deployment as resolution.
- Defer any TUI until observed operational pain requires persistent selection/live refresh; metric visualization remains dashboard territory.

All implementation follows repository Definition of Done and updates tests/docs for each changed public contract.

title: Add interactive sync status command
description:
Add report-only `jernerics interactive sync status --backend NAME [--json]`.

Inspect the current project's named Mutagen session without creating, restarting, terminating, flushing, copying, or invoking one-shot fallback. Human output reports session name, raw Mutagen status, local/cluster endpoint connectivity, idle/converged state, conflict count, and conflicted relative paths. Use local/cluster vocabulary, not Mutagen alpha/beta, in the public output.

JSON contract includes project, backend, session, exists, status (nullable when missing), local_connected, cluster_connected, idle, converged, conflicts, and conflicted_paths. A successfully inspected missing, disconnected, syncing, or conflicted session exits zero; state is data. Exit nonzero only when configuration or Mutagen prevents inspection. Missing session returns exists=false, nullable endpoint/status fields, false idle/converged, zero conflicts, and an empty path list.

Reuse current SessionInfo/is_idle/is_converged/conflicted_paths logic and the existing warning policy. Do not alter normal interactive start conflict behavior.

title: Add safe interactive sync conflict resolver
description:
Add explicit conflict resolution:
`jernerics interactive sync resolve PATH... --backend NAME --from local|cluster [--dry-run] [--yes]`.

Scope and preflight:
- Require one or more explicit relative paths; no --all.
- One source applies to the invocation; mixed winners use separate invocations.
- Every selected path must be in the session's current Mutagen conflict list.
- Both endpoint entries must exist and be regular files. Refuse missing paths, directories, symlinks, type changes, unsafe traversal, or paths outside either project root.
- Never infer a winner from mtime or content.
- Preview every path, direction, size, endpoint checksum, and backup destination. Prompt once. --dry-run exits after validation/preview without backup or mutation. Noninteractive mutation requires --yes.

Backup and mutation:
- Store every losing copy locally under $XDG_STATE_HOME/jernerics/sync-backups/<project>/<UTC-unique-run>/, default ~/.local/state. Cluster losers download directly; create no persistent cluster backup.
- Write manifest.json with session, endpoints, source, selected paths, original and backup checksums, timestamps, and per-path results. Never auto-delete backups.
- Complete and checksum-verify all backups before the first overwrite. If local storage is insufficient or backup fails, mutate nothing.
- Re-hash source and destination immediately before each mutation; abort on changes.
- Process one path at a time. Transfer to a temporary sibling on the destination, verify checksum, atomically replace the loser, and remove temporary data. Peak destination temporary storage is one file; refuse before replacement if unavailable.
- On any copy/verification failure, stop immediately, never auto-rollback, and report completed, untouched, and unresolved paths plus the backup directory.
- Flush the existing Mutagen session, wait for idle, re-read conflicts, and require every selected path to disappear. Unselected conflicts may remain.
- Never restart/replace the Mutagen session and never invoke one-shot ProjectSync as resolution.

Verification must use isolated temporary Mutagen sessions/directories, not the live symlab session. Cover local winner, cluster winner, multiple explicit paths, mixed remaining conflicts, dry-run, refusal shapes, source/destination races, backup/download failure, temporary transfer failure, partial completion reporting, and conflict-clear verification.

Acceptance: focused unit and isolated end-to-end resolution scenarios pass, backup recovery evidence is verified, full Definition of Done passes, and changed files staged.

Verified via 42 focused tests + orchestrator-run isolated Mutagen e2e (dry-run/refusal/local-wins/cluster-wins/mixed/no-yes/staging-cleanup); 761 full green. title: Define backend-neutral trial tracker primitives
description:
## Problem

Commit `af94fba` expanded `ConsoleTracker` to mirror `JsonlTracker` methods (`log_json`, `log_artifact`, `log_sweep_meta`) after standalone trial scripts crashed. Mirroring the backend surface is the wrong boundary: job mode exposes backend-only methods that standalone mode cannot reliably match.

## Locked design

The trial-facing protocol has four backend-neutral operations:

- `log_param(key, value)` for scalar experiment configuration.
- `log_value(key, value, *, step: int | None = None)` for any small JSON-compatible observation. `step` is special event metadata: an optional caller-supplied ordinal in a repeated measurement series, not specifically a deep-learning optimizer step.
- `log_artifact(key, path)` for externally materialized files requiring retention/transfer.
- `finish(results)` for terminal JSON-compatible results and lifecycle completion.

`log_text` and `log_json` are not separate trial primitives; strings and structured values use `log_value`. `log_sweep_meta`, `context`, `close`, context-manager methods, and writer details remain backend/runner internals.

Job and standalone modes must expose the same runtime surface. Implement the job tracker as a small adapter around `JsonlTracker`, not by inheriting and leaking its full method set. The adapter dispatches numeric observations to `JsonlTracker.log_value` and other JSON-compatible observations to `JsonlTracker.log_json`, preserving optional `step`.

## Changes

Jernerics:

- Revert commit `af94fba` with `git revert af94fba`.
- Update `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/trial_context.py` with the four-method protocol, JSON-compatible value typing, bounded `ConsoleTracker`, and composed job adapter.
- Update `packages/jernerics/tests/unit/test_trial_context.py` for standalone/job numeric and structured values, optional step, artifact events/manifests, finish behavior, and absence of backend-only methods.
- Leave the low-level `JsonlTracker` API intact unless a minimal annotation-only change is required.

Symlab:

- Change `experiments/overfit/trial.py` from `tracker.log_json("pred_expr", pred_expr, step=step)` to `tracker.log_value("pred_expr", pred_expr, step=step)`.
- Existing `log_artifact` calls remain valid.

## Acceptance

- `ConsoleTracker` and the job adapter support the same four public operations.
- Numeric and structured observations preserve their values and optional `step` in JSONL output.
- Artifact logging writes the event and job-mode manifest; standalone mode prints the key/path.
- Trial code cannot rely on `log_text`, `log_json`, or `log_sweep_meta` through the trial-facing object.
- Standalone and temporary job-mode smoke scenarios succeed.
- From `/home/jerry/Projects/jernerics`, `nix develop --command just check` passes without creating a `.venv`.
- The symlab migration receives a focused Nix-based syntax/lint check without creating a `.venv`.
- Commit history contains the explicit revert and a clear design-decision commit; the separate symlab repository receives its own migration commit.

title: Interactive: tmux panes drop /opt/venv, torch import fails (login-shell PATH reset)
description:
## Problem

`jernerics interactive` drops the user into an `apptainer shell` inside `container.sif`. The first shell has `/opt/venv/bin` on `PATH` (set by `%environment` / `ENV`), so `import torch` works. But the moment the user starts `tmux` for session persistence — which the design explicitly recommends (`interactive.py:10-13`: "Process persistence (tmux, screen, etc.) is left to the user") — every pane is a **login** shell that sources `/etc/profile`, which resets `PATH` to the Debian default and drops `/opt/venv/bin`. `python` then resolves to the container's base `/usr/bin/python3` (no torch) → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'`.

Confirmed on gpu29 (UConn HPC): `shopt -q login_shell` → LOGIN; `env` diff shows the pane `PATH` losing `/opt/venv/bin` and gaining the exact Debian `/etc/profile` default, and `PS1` reverting from `Apptainer>` to the host Debian prompt.

## Root cause

The container templates (`templates/python.def`, `templates/python.Dockerfile`) put `/opt/venv/bin` on `PATH` **only** via `%environment` (Apptainer) / `ENV` (Docker). These run once at container entry, never in subshells. Login subshells (tmux panes) re-run `/etc/profile` and wipe it. This contradicts the interactive feature's own guidance to use tmux — i.e. the recommended persistence workflow is broken by construction.

`PYTHONPATH` survives (inherited, not reset by `/etc/profile`); only `PATH` is clobbered, so only the venv resolution breaks.

## Fix

Bake `/opt/venv` activation into `/etc/profile.d/jernerics.sh` (installed in `%post` / `RUN`) so every login subshell re-acquires it; also source it from `/etc/bash.bashrc` for non-login interactive panes. Keep `%environment` / `ENV` for the entry shell.

```
if [ -d /opt/venv/bin ]; then
    case ":${PATH:-}:" in
        *:/opt/venv/bin:*) ;;
        *) export PATH="/opt/venv/bin:${PATH:-}" ;;
    esac
    export VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
fi
```

## Files

- `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/templates/python.def` (add to `%post`)
- `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/templates/python.Dockerfile` (add `RUN`)
- `packages/jernerics/tests/unit/container/test_starters.py` (assert activation present)
- `example/container.def`, `example/Dockerfile` (sync committed copies)

## Acceptance

- New assertion in `test_starters.py` passes: both starters contain login-shell venv activation (`/etc/profile.d` referencing `/opt/venv`).
- Manual on HPC: rebuild container → `jernerics interactive` → `tmux` → `python -c "import torch"` succeeds.

## Caveat

Existing `container.sif` must be rebuilt to pick this up. Worse, `jernerics-dsj` (build marker doesn't hash `container.def`) means the rebuild may not auto-trigger — users may need `--force`.

title: Container build should auto-discover workspace packages
description:
## Problem
The container.def requires manually listing each workspace package directory in %files. When a new package is added to the workspace (e.g., experiments/latent_smc), it must be manually added to container.def or it won't be included in the build. This is fragile and easy to forget.

## Expected behavior
`jernerics build` should auto-discover all workspace packages from the root pyproject.toml and include them in the container build automatically — just like `uv sync --all-packages` does locally.

## Current behavior
Only explicitly listed directories in container.def %files are included. The build uses `uv sync --no-dev --no-editable` (not --all-packages), so workspace sub-packages and their dependencies are not installed.

## Workaround
Manually add each new workspace package to container.def %files and change uv sync to --all-packages.

title: Interactive HPC sessions with continuous code sync
description:
# Interactive HPC Sessions

## Problem
Currently jernerics only supports batch job submission (`jernerics run`). There is no way to get an interactive shell on a GPU node for exploratory work (marimo notebooks, debugging, ad-hoc experiments). Users must manually manage SLURM allocations, SSH connections, and code syncing.

## Solution
`jernerics interactive` — a command that handles the full lifecycle of an interactive GPU session:

1. **Allocate** a GPU via sbatch reservation job (survives SSH disconnect)
2. **Sync** code continuously via mutagen (bidirectional, local stays source of truth)
3. **Connect** via SSH ProxyJump + tmux (reconnectable, terminal state preserved)

## Key design decisions

### Allocation strategy: sbatch + SSH (not srun --pty)
- `srun --pty` dies when SSH drops → allocation lost
- `sbatch` reservation job (sleep infinity) survives disconnect → reconnect later
- SSH to compute node via ProxyJump through login node
- Cluster uses `pam_slurm_adopt.so` — SSH to compute nodes works only with active job (verified)

### Code sync: mutagen (not for batch jobs)
- Batch jobs keep existing tar+scp (synchronous, zero-dep, stable)
- Interactive uses mutagen for continuous bidirectional sync
- Mutagen agent auto-injected via SSH (no remote install needed)
- NFS home dirs require `--watch-mode=portable` (polling, ~10s for HPC→local)
- Local filesystem watching is real-time (local→HPC is instant)
- `--ignore-vcs` — git operations only local
- `--sync-mode two-way-safe` — conflicts surfaced, not silently overwritten

### Shell: tmux on compute node (inside container)
- tmux session preserves terminal state across reconnects
- `tmux new -s jernerics || tmux attach -t jernerics` pattern
- User dropped into container shell (apptainer shell) at /work/<project>
- Container has: PYTHONPATH set, marimo available, GPU access
- tmux needs to be installed in container (currently missing)

### Reconnect: detect existing allocation
- `squeue --name=jernerics-interactive-<project> --me`
- Found + RUNNING → parse node hostname, reattach tmux, resume sync
- Not found → new session path

## Cluster specifics (UConn HPC, verified Aug 2026)
- Login node: `hpc2.storrs.hpc.uconn.edu` (round-robin, resolves to login5 etc)
- Compute nodes: gpu13-gpu30 in general-gpu partition
- SSH to compute nodes: works via ProxyJump, gated by pam_slurm_adopt
- NFS home: auto.home on /home (autofs), wekafs backing store
- tmux: on login nodes (v2.7), NOT in container (needs adding)
- mutagen: not installed locally or on HPC (agent auto-injects)
- Container: PYTHONPATH=/work/libs/symbolic/src:/work/models/manifest/src, marimo at /opt/venv/bin/marimo

title: Interactive allocation + reconnectable shell (sbatch + SSH ProxyJump + tmux)
description:
## Goal
Implement `jernerics interactive --backend hpc` that allocates a GPU, connects you to a shell inside the container on the compute node, with tmux for session persistence.

## Architecture

### New CLI command: `jernerics interactive`
```
jernerics interactive --backend hpc [--time 4:00:00] [--gpus 1] [--partition general-gpu] [--constraint a100]
jernerics interactive --backend hpc (reconnects if existing session found)
jernerics interactive --end --backend hpc (explicit teardown)
```

### Flow
1. **Check for existing session**: `squeue --name=jernerics-interactive-<project> --me --states=R`
   - Found → RECONNECT path (skip to step 4)
   - Not found → NEW session path
2. **NEW session**: 
   - Generate SBATCH script: `sleep infinity` with `--partition`, `--gres=gpu:N`, `--constraint`, `--time`, `--job-name=jernerics-interactive-<project>`
   - Submit via existing `host.run([sbatch --parsable])` pattern
   - Poll `squeue --job <id>` until state=RUNNING
   - Parse node hostname from `NodeList` column
3. **Start sync** (hook point — task 2 fills this in, no-op stub for now)
4. **Connect to shell**:
   - `ssh -J <login_host> <user>@<compute_node>` 
   - Inside SSH: `apptainer shell --nv -B <remote_dir>:/work <container.sif>`
   - Inside container: `cd /work/<project> && tmux new -s jernerics || tmux attach -t jernerics`
   - This should use PTY mode (subprocess with pty) to give interactive terminal
5. **On disconnect** (SSH dies, Ctrl+D): print message that job is still running, show reconnect command
6. **Teardown** (`--end` flag or `scancel`):
   - `scancel <job_id>`
   - Call sync cleanup hook
   - Print summary

### Config additions
```toml
[tool.jernerics.backends.hpc.interactive]
time = "4:00:00"       # default walltime
gpus = 1               # default GPU count
tmux_session = "jernerics"  # tmux session name
```

### Implementation location
- New module: `jernerics/backend/slurm/interactive.py` — allocation logic, SSH command construction
- CLI: add `interactive` command to `cli.py`
- Reuse: `SSHHost` from `host.py`, config loading from `config.py`

### Key details
- **pam_slurm_adopt**: SSH to compute nodes only works with active job. Verified on cluster.
- **ProxyJump**: `ssh -o ProxyJump=<user>@hpc2.storrs.hpc.uconn.edu <user>@<gpu_node>`
- **Container entry**: must use `apptainer shell` (not exec) for interactive shell. Need `-B <remote_dir>:/work` bind mount.
- **tmux**: currently NOT in container.def. Either add to container build OR use host tmux (available on login/compute nodes at /usr/bin/tmux, accessible inside container via apptainer default bind mounts). Test which works.
- **PTY**: the SSH command needs a real PTY. Use `subprocess` with `pty=True` or `pexpect`.

### Tests
- Unit: SBATCH script generation, squeue output parsing, node hostname extraction
- Unit: reconnect detection logic (mock squeue output)
- Integration (manual): full e2e on HPC

### Dependencies
- None blocking (task 2 can run in parallel, sync is a hook point)
notes:
Implemented on branch `interactive-shell` (commit 2fb661a). `just check` passes (lint+format+typecheck; 558 tests pass, +34 new).

## Delivered
- New module `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/backend/slurm/interactive.py`:
  - `format_interactive_script()` — renders the `sleep infinity` sbatch reservation script (job-name, partition, time, mem, cpus, --gres=gpu:N, optional --constraint), with SLURM value validation.
  - `extract_node()` / `parse_session_lines()` — squeue `%i|%T|%N` parsing + node hostname extraction (header-skip, pending=empty-node, multi-node takes first).
  - `InteractiveSession` — find_existing (reconnect detection by job name), submit, wait_for_running (poll until RUNNING, terminal-state + timeout errors), ssh_argv/remote_shell_command (ProxyJump + host-tmux-wraps-`apptainer shell`), connect (raw ssh -t, inherits PTY), end (scancel).

- **Allocation**: sbatch `sleep infinity` reservation (survives SSH disconnect) rather than `srun --pty`.
- **Reconnect shell**: host `tmux new-session -A` wraps `apptainer shell`. Host tmux keeps the apptainer shell alive across SSH drops; `-A` reattaches on reconnect, creates (re-running apptainer shell) otherwise. Uses `apptainer shell` per spec; tmux on the host (robust reconnect semantics). Binds remote_dir:/work + cache:/cache.
- **PTY**: connect() runs `ssh -t` directly (bypasses SSHHost capture) so the terminal is interactive.
- **Sync**: marked as a no-op hook point in `_interactive_connect` for task uyy.2; not implemented here.

- Dry-run smoke test against a dummy project: SBATCH directives and ssh/tmux command resolve correctly (interactive time overrides slurm; ~ and user extracted from host; nested shlex quoting correct).

title: Continuous bidirectional code sync via mutagen for interactive sessions
description:
## Goal
Implement continuous bidirectional code sync between local project dir and HPC using mutagen, integrated with the interactive session lifecycle.

## Architecture

### New module: `jernerics/sync/mutagen_sync.py`
```python
class MutagenSync:
    """Wraps mutagen CLI for continuous bidirectional sync."""

    def start(self, local_dir: Path, remote_host: str, remote_dir: str,
              excludes: list[str]) -> str:
        """Create mutagen sync session. Returns session name.
        Blocks until initial convergence."""

    def wait_converged(self, session_name: str, timeout: int = 60) -> bool:
        """Poll until initial sync complete."""

    def terminate(self, session_name: str) -> None:
        """Terminate and clean up sync session."""

    def list_sessions(self) -> list[dict]:
        """List active sync sessions (for orphan detection)."""
```

### Mutagen command construction
```bash
mutagen sync create <local_dir> <user>@<host>:<remote_dir> \
    --name jernerics-<project>-interactive \
    --ignore-vcs \
    --watch-mode portable \
    --sync-mode two-way-safe \
    -i "results/" -i "pools/" -i ".venv/" -i "__pycache__/" \
    -i "*.pyc" -i ".cache/" -i "*.egg-info/" -i "container.sif" \
    -i "logs/" -i "*.sif"
```

### Sync protocol (abstraction for future extensibility)
```python
class Sync(Protocol):
    def sync(self, project_dir: Path, remote_dir: str) -> None: ...

class OneShotSync(Sync):   # existing tar+scp (ProjectSync), for batch
    ...

class ContinuousSync(Sync): # mutagen wrapper, for interactive
    def start(self, ...) -> str: ...
    def stop(self) -> None: ...
```

### Integration with interactive lifecycle
- Task 1 (interactive shell) provides hook points: sync.start() after allocation, sync.stop() before/after teardown
- Session naming: jernerics-<project>-interactive (matches SLURM job name pattern)
- On reconnect: check if mutagen session exists (mutagen sync list), resume if so

### Dependency handling
- mutagen is an optional dependency: check shutil.which("mutagen") at runtime
- If not found: print install instructions, fall back to existing tar+scp for initial sync, warn that continuous sync is unavailable
- Do NOT make mutagen a hard dependency of jernerics

### NFS considerations (verified on UConn HPC)
- Home dir is autofs + wekafs NFS, inotify does not work
- Must use --watch-mode portable (polling, 10s default interval)
- HPC->local sync has ~10s latency (notebook edits flow back slowly)
- Local->HPC sync is real-time (local filesystem watching works normally)
- Mutagen syncs to login node; compute nodes see files via shared NFS mount

### Orphan detection
- On jernerics interactive startup: mutagen sync list for sessions matching jernerics-*
- If found with no matching SLURM job: offer to terminate stale session

### Tests
- Unit: mutagen command construction, session name generation
- Unit: exclude pattern list
- Unit: convergence polling logic (mock mutagen sync list output)
- Integration (manual): create session, verify files sync bidirectionally

### Prerequisites
- Install mutagen locally (brew install mutagen-io/mutagen/mutagen on macOS or download from mutagen.io)
- No HPC-side installation needed (agent auto-injection)
notes:
Implemented in commit a137537 on branch interactive-sync (worktree /tmp/wt-interactive-sync).

Delivered: jernerics/sync/mutagen_sync.py + 41 unit tests (tests/unit/sync/test_mutagen_sync.py).

Design decisions / deviations from the task draft:
- Module placed at jernerics/sync/mutagen_sync.py as specified. Package docstring disambiguates it from the 'jernerics sync' CLI command (replay) and the tracking stream per CONTEXT.md.
- Did NOT build the proposed Sync/OneShotSync/ContinuousSync Protocol. It is speculative (vision non-goal: no speculative features) AND internally inconsistent — ContinuousSync has start()/stop(), not sync(), so it could not satisfy the Protocol. MutagenSync is a focused class instead; the interactive command (task .1) will dispatch between MutagenSync and ProjectSync via MutagenSync.available().
- Corrected mutagen flags from the draft: the CLI uses -m/--mode (draft said --sync-mode). Verified against mutagen 0.18.1.
- Session naming uses jernerics-interactive-<project> (matching task .1's SLURM job-name pattern), NOT the draft's jernerics-<project>-interactive. The draft text and task .1 disagreed; chose the form that lets orphan detection pair a sync session with its job. SESSION_PREFIX is a single constant, trivial to flip.
- list_sessions filters client-side: mutagen 'sync list <name>' errors (exit 1) on a missing name, which would break convergence polling.
- terminate is idempotent (swallows 'did not match any sessions') so teardown never fails on an already-ended session.
- No CLI command added — the interactive lifecycle (task .1) is the trigger and is not yet built. Orphan helpers (find_orphans/terminate_orphans) are ready for it to call.

Verification: just check green (lint + format-check + typecheck + 565 passed/6 skipped). End-to-end smoke test against real mutagen 0.18.1: build_create_command's exact flag set accepted, bidirectional transfer works, 17 ignore patterns honored, list/wait_converged/terminate/orphan all correct against live sessions.

No HPC-side integration yet (needs task .1's interactive command). Left on branch for review; not merged.

title: E2E integration: wire mutagen sync into interactive lifecycle + verify on HPC
description:
## Goal
Wire the mutagen sync module (uyy.2) into the interactive command lifecycle (uyy.1), then verify the full flow end-to-end on the UConn HPC cluster.

## Part 1: Code integration

The hook point is in cli.py line 380 (`_interactive_connect`). Currently a no-op comment. Wire in MutagenSync:

### On new session (after allocation, before connect):
```python
sync = MutagenSync(local_dir=project_dir, remote_host=host, remote_dir=remote_dir)
if sync.available():
    name = sync.start()  # blocks until converged
    sync.wait_converged(name)
```

### On reconnect:
```python
# Check if mutagen session exists, resume if so
sessions = sync.list_sessions(name=sync.session_name(project_name))
if not sessions:
    # Session died, restart it
    sync.start()
```

### On teardown (--end):
```python
sync.terminate(sync.session_name(project_name))
session.end()  # scancel
```

### On orphan detection (startup):
```python
orphans = sync.find_orphans()
if orphans:
    # Print warning, offer to clean up
```

### Graceful fallback (mutagen not installed):
```python
if not MutagenSync.available():
    print("Warning: mutagen not found. Using one-shot sync.")
    # Fall back to ProjectSync.sync_project() for initial push
    # No continuous sync available
```

## Part 2: E2E verification on HPC

Test the complete flow manually against the real cluster:

1. `jernerics interactive --backend hpc --dry-run` — verify sbatch script + ssh command
2. `jernerics interactive --backend hpc` — full new session:
   - Job submits, waits for RUNNING, parses node
   - Mutagen sync starts, converges
   - Shell opens in container with tmux
3. Edit a file locally → verify it appears on HPC within 1-2s
4. Edit a file on HPC (inside container) → verify it flows back within ~10s
5. Ctrl+D (disconnect) → verify job keeps running, mutagen keeps syncing
6. `jernerics interactive --backend hpc` (reconnect) → verify tmux reattach
7. `jernerics interactive --backend hpc --end` → verify scancel + mutagen terminate
8. Start session, kill mutagen daemon, reconnect → verify orphan detection + restart

- Login: jez21005@hpc2.storrs.hpc.uconn.edu
- Partition: general-gpu, constraint: a100
- Container: ~/projects/symlab-overfit/container.sif (has tmux)
- Mutagen needs --watch-mode portable (NFS home)
- pam_slurm_adopt gates SSH to compute nodes

- Tasks .1 and .2 are merged. This task builds on both.

title: Add jernerics replay CLI command for syncing unsynced tracking events
description:
## Problem

`replay_tracking()` exists in `tracking/batch_sync.py` and works — it ships local `.jsonl` event files to the HTTP tracking server idempotently (INSERT OR IGNORE). But it is only callable from `local_backend.py` (after local runs) and `post_hook.py` (SLURM post-hook chain). There is no CLI surface.

When tracking events dont reach the server (e.g. compute nodes cant reach the server, or a run was killed before post-hook fired), there is no way to manually push the unsynced events.

## Design

Add a `jernerics replay` CLI command that wraps `replay_tracking()`.

### Interface

```bash
# Replay all unsynced events for the current project
jernerics replay

# Scope to a specific study
jernerics replay --study <study_name>

# Custom tracking dir (e.g. SCP-ed from HPC)
jernerics replay --tracking-dir /tmp/symlab-tracking

# Override server
jernerics replay --server https://atlas.taile454b.ts.net

# Dry run — hits server to compare, reports gaps, does NOT send
jernerics replay --dry-run

# JSON output
jernerics replay --json
```

### Flag resolution

| Flag | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `--tracking-dir` | `cache_dir()/tracking/` | Resolved via hierarchical config (jyl.7) |
| `--server` | `[tool.jernerics] tracking_server` or `JERNERICS_TRACKING_SERVER` env | Same as load_tracking_server() |
| `--study` | All studies | Optional scoping |
| `--dry-run` | False | Hits server /query to count existing events per study, compares against local .jsonl counts, reports "X local, Y already synced, Z would be new". Does NOT send events. |
| `--json` | False | Machine-readable output |

### Dry-run behavior (agreed with Jerry)

Dry-run hits the server. It queries `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE study_name = ?` per study via `/query`, compares against local `.jsonl` event counts, and reports the delta. This tells you what is actually missing, not just what is local.

## Implementation notes

- Thin wrapper — `replay_tracking()` already does all the work
- Resolve `tracking_dir` from `cache_dir()` (which will use hierarchical config after jyl.7)
- Resolve `base_url` from `load_tracking_server()`
- ~30-50 lines of CLI code + tests
- Follow existing CLI patterns in `cli.py` (Typer annotations, Annotated types)

## Test plan

- Unit: mock `replay_tracking`, verify CLI resolves correct tracking_dir and server URL
- Unit: dry-run queries server, computes deltas correctly
- Integration: create temp .jsonl files, replay against a real test server

## Definition of done

1. `just check` passes
2. `just typecheck` passes
3. Commit: `feat(cli): add jernerics replay command (jernerics-jyl.12)`

title: Design context-dimension tracking model
description:
## LOCKED SPEC: Context-dimension tracking model

All design decisions resolved. Reviewed by second agent (OMP). All 9 review findings accepted.

### Final schema

```sql
-- Schema version
PRAGMA user_version = 2;

-- Tracked values: scalar + json unified. Artifacts stay separate.
CREATE TABLE tracked_values (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    run_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    key TEXT NOT NULL,
    step INTEGER,
    context TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    value_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
        (value_type = 'scalar' AND scalar_val IS NOT NULL AND text_val IS NULL)
        OR (value_type = 'json' AND text_val IS NOT NULL AND scalar_val IS NULL)
    ),
    scalar_val REAL,
    text_val TEXT,
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, run_id, seq)
) STRICT;

CREATE INDEX idx_values_study_key ON tracked_values(project, study_name, key);
CREATE INDEX idx_values_study_key_step ON tracked_values(project, study_name, key, step);

-- Params: separate table, typed columns (set once per trial by Optuna)
CREATE TABLE params (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    key TEXT NOT NULL,
    float_val REAL,
    int_val INTEGER,
    string_val TEXT,
    bool_val INTEGER,
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, key)
) STRICT;

-- Artifacts: separate table (different access pattern, file references)
CREATE TABLE artifacts (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    run_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    key TEXT NOT NULL,
    context TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    filename TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, run_id, seq)
) STRICT;

-- Sweep provenance (unchanged)
CREATE TABLE sweep_meta (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    git_hash TEXT,
    config TEXT,
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, seq)
) STRICT;

-- Trial lifecycle marker (unchanged)
CREATE TABLE trial_end (
    project TEXT NOT NULL,
    study_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    trial_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    timestamp_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (project, study_name, trial_id, seq)
) STRICT;
```

### Key design decisions (locked)

1. **Context storage**: JSON TEXT column. Always serialize with `json.dumps(context, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))` in the tracker — single chokepoint.
2. **Unified values table**: scalar + json only. Artifacts separate. value_type CHECK constraint enforces column consistency.
3. **Params separate table**: UNIQUE on (project, study_name, trial_id, key) with INSERT OR REPLACE for upsert. Params JOINed as pseudo-dimensions at query time.
4. **step as reserved INTEGER column**: nullable, indexable. Not privileged (context still carries seed/fold/etc), but first-class for the 80% "loss vs step" query. step IS NULL = non-time-series value.
5. **run_id column**: assigned per tracker instantiation. Included in UNIQUE. Fixes multi-seed/re-run/concurrent-writer collisions.
6. **Fresh start migration**: drop old tables, create new schema, bump PRAGMA user_version to 2.
7. **Secondary indexes**: (project, study_name, key) and (project, study_name, key, step) on tracked_values.

### Tracker API

```python
tracker.log_value("loss", 0.32, step=100, context={"seed": 3})
tracker.log_value("test_accuracy", 0.91)  # step IS NULL = non-time-series
tracker.log_value("confusion_matrix", {...})  # dict → json storage
tracker.log_artifact("plot.png", "/path/to/plot.png", context={"seed": 3})
tracker.log_param("lr", 0.01)  # unchanged, upserts
```

Type inference rules (in order):
1. Check bool BEFORE int (isinstance(True, int) is True)
2. Coerce numpy types: np.float64 → float, np.int32 → int via numbers.Real/numbers.Integral or explicit float()/int()
3. Handle NaN/Inf: coerce to NULL with a warning, or sanitize at serialization
4. int/float → value_type='scalar', scalar_val
5. dict/list → value_type='json', text_val (json.dumps)
6. str → not supported in log_value (use log_result or wrap in dict)

### Envelope changes

The JSONL envelope must carry the unified payload. New shape:

```python
class ValueEvent(TypedDict, total=False):
    key: str
    value: float | str  # scalar value or JSON string
    step: int | None
    context: dict  # arbitrary dimensions

class Envelope(TypedDict, total=False):
    project: str
    study_name: str
    trial_id: int
    run_id: int  # NEW
    timestamp_ns: int
    seq: int
    value: ValueEvent       # replaces metric + result
    param: ParamEvent       # unchanged
    artifact: ArtifactEvent # now carries context
    sweep_meta: SweepMetaEvent
    trial_end: TrialEndEvent
```

### Files to modify

1. `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/store.py` — new schema, new insert dispatch
2. `packages/jernerics-server/src/jernerics_server/http.py` — no endpoint changes, but MAX_ROWS may need increasing
3. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/envelope.py` — new envelope shapes
4. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/tracker.py` — new API (log_value, log_artifact with context, log_param unchanged)
5. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/jsonl_io.py` — may need updates for new envelope
6. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/stream_client.py` — no changes (ships envelopes generically)
7. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/batch_sync.py` — artifact sync path cleanup (issue .2 overlaps)
8. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/runner.py` — run_id assignment
9. `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/tracking/trial_environment.py` — run_id propagation
10. All test files under `tests/unit/tracking/` — update for new API
11. `example/trial.py` — update to new API

title: Design analysis/exploration layer
description:
Design how analysis and monitoring work on top of the context-dimension model. Two distinct use cases:

1. MONITORING — 'is my job alive, is training diverging, show me that artifact' — real-time, glanceable, high-frequency. Open → scan → close.

2. ANALYSIS — 'which trials should I care about, how does this compare to last week' — post-hoc, comparative, exploratory. Explore → drill → compare → decide.

Key constraint: must not become a maintenance burden. The old React SPA (jernerics-dashboard) was a full frontend stack — too heavy.

Direction from research:
- Grafana Metrics Drilldown pattern: queryless exploration where the data's own structure IS the navigation (discover dimensions from data, show breakdowns per label value, click to filter)
- No pre-declaration needed — dimension-type heuristics infer role (numeric monotonic → x-axis candidate, low cardinality → grouping, etc.)
- Grafana itself is a poor fit (Prometheus cardinality, time-as-x-axis assumption, wrong query patterns)
- Start with /query (SQL endpoint) before building any UI

Options to evaluate:
A. Start with no dashboard — analysis via notebook/CLI against /query
B. Build minimal exploration tool later (lightweight, not full SPA)
C. Use Grafana for live monitoring only (thin exporter for active runs)
close_reason: Design completed. Decisions: (1) Analysis functions query Store directly, no decoupling layer. (2) Generic computational primitives (first→last, change, early/recent slope), not ML-specific assertions like 'plateaued'. (3) Three CLI commands: jernerics runs, summary, diff. watch deferred. (4) All params shown, no filtering. (5) rich for formatting. (6) Every metric treated identically — no semantic grouping. (7) Slope windows: first 10% vs last 10%, min 5 points, step ranges in header. (8) diff uses final values only, not trajectory shape. (9) --json flag for agent consumption, same data, raw values (not human-formatted). (10) Agent guidance to dig deeper lives in skill, not tool logic.

title: Hierarchical jernerics config resolution across nested pyproject.toml
description:
## Problem

`find_pyproject_dir()` walks up from cwd and stops at the FIRST pyproject.toml. In uv workspaces with experiment subpackages (e.g. symlab/experiments/probe/pyproject.toml), this shadows the project root and breaks:

- Project name resolution (gets "probe" instead of "symlab")
- `cache_dir()` paths (~/.cache/jernerics/probe/ instead of symlab/)
- Tracking server URL (not found → empty → "Request URL missing protocol")
- `[tool.jernerics]` backend config lookup

## Root cause

`config.py::find_pyproject_dir()` returns the nearest pyproject.toml, not the one that owns jernerics config.

## Design: hierarchical config

Implement a merge-based config system:

1. **Root detection** — the topmost pyproject.toml containing `[tool.jernerics]` is the root. Project name always comes from root.
2. **Deep merge** — nested pyproject.toml files with `[tool.jernerics]` override root settings. E.g. experiments/probe/pyproject.toml can override `backends.hpc.remote_dir` without redefining the full config.
3. **Backward compatible** — if no nested `[tool.jernerics]` exists, behavior is unchanged.

## Touchpoints

- `config.py` — `find_pyproject_dir()`, `get_project_name()`, config loading
- `paths.py` — `cache_dir()` uses project name
- All callers of `find_pyproject_dir()`

## Symlab-side (separate, no beads task)

After the jernerics fix lands, remove unnecessary pyproject.toml from experiment subpackages OR add `[tool.jernerics]` overrides where experiment-specific config makes sense.

## Test plan

- Unit: nested pyproject with/without [tool.jernerics], deep merge correctness, root detection
- Integration: run `jernerics logs`, `jernerics runs` from a nested experiment dir — resolves root config correctly

Retried trials lose server_addr — tracking streams fail on retry
description:
## Problem

When a trial is retried (via the checker/heartbeat mechanism), the retry context (`ctx.json`) does not persist `server_addr`. The resubmitted trial runs with a schemeless tracking URL, causing `httpx.UnsupportedProtocol: Request URL is missing an 'http://' or 'https://' protocol`.

The fresh-submission path is unaffected — only retried trials lose the tracking server address.

## Reproduction

1. Submit a job to HPC with `JERNERICS_TRACKING_SERVER` set
2. Kill the trial mid-run (or let the heartbeat go stale) to trigger a retry
3. The retried trial's tracking events fail to stream — `Failed to send event, retry 1/2/3...`

## Root cause

The retry context serialization (`ctx.json`) doesn't include `server_addr`, so when the checker resubmits the trial, the env var is missing.

## Fix

Persist `server_addr` in the retry context alongside other fields, and restore it when resubmitting.

title: logs --follow blocks indefinitely, agents resort to sleep loops
description:
## Problem

`jernerics logs --backend hpc <job_id> --follow` blocks the terminal until the job reaches a terminal state. For Slurm, it spawns `tail -f` via SSH and calls `wait_for_completion(poll_interval=10)` internally — it does return when the job finishes, but:

1. It blocks for the entire job duration (could be hours)
2. Agent sessions with timeouts get killed mid-follow
3. The SSH tail connection can drop, leaving the process hanging
4. Agents can't do other work while blocked

As a result, agents (OMP, Hermes) skip `--follow` entirely and resort to `sleep N && jernerics jobs --backend hpc` polling loops. This is wasteful and fragile.

## Current behavior

```
# After jernerics run, the CLI prints:
#   jernerics logs --backend hpc <job_id> --follow

# But agents do this instead:
sleep 30 && jernerics jobs --backend hpc
sleep 60 && jernerics jobs --backend hpc
# ... repeat until COMPLETED
```

## Proposed solution

Add a `--wait` / `--timeout` option to `jernerics logs` (or a new `jernerics wait` command) that:

- Polls job status at a configurable interval (default 10s)
- Returns immediately if the job is already in a terminal state
- Returns with exit code 0 if COMPLETED, non-zero if FAILED or TIMEOUT
- Accepts `--timeout <seconds>` — returns after N seconds if job hasn't finished yet, printing partial logs
- Does NOT spawn `tail -f` — instead polls log content incrementally and prints new lines since last poll

This would let agents do:
```
jernerics wait --backend hpc <job_id> --timeout 60  # poll for 60s
# ... do other work ...
jernerics wait --backend hpc <job_id> --timeout 60  # poll again
```

Or just:
```
jernerics wait --backend hpc <job_id>  # blocks until done, no timeout
```

The difference from `--follow` is that `--wait` uses polling internally (resilient to SSH drops) and supports `--timeout` for bounded waits.

title: Script-as-trial: new trial context API (trial_config, trial_tracker, is_job, ConsoleTracker)
description:
## Scope

Create a NEW module that provides the script-as-trial API. This is purely additive — do NOT modify the runner or existing trial execution path. Nothing existing should break.

## CRITICAL: No backward compatibility

This task is part of a breaking change. Do NOT add any backward compatibility shims, legacy function import fallbacks, or deprecation warnings. The old `def trial(config, tracker)` pattern will be removed in a subsequent task. This task only adds the new API.

## API

New module: `packages/jernerics/src/jernerics/trial_context.py`

### is_job() -> bool
- Returns `True` if `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var is set
- This means the script is running as a scheduled job via jernerics runner
- Returns `False` when running standalone (e.g., `python trial.py`)

### trial_config(defaults: dict | None = None) -> dict
- **Job mode** (`is_job()` is True): reads JSON from `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` env var, returns parsed dict
- **Standalone mode** (`is_job()` is False): returns the `defaults` dict as-is
- Raises `RuntimeError` if job mode but env var points to missing/unreadable file
- Raises `ValueError` if standalone mode and `defaults` is None

### trial_tracker() -> Tracker | ConsoleTracker
- **Job mode:** returns a real `Tracker` configured from env vars (same env vars the runner already sets for the current tracker — check `tracking/trial_environment.py` for what is available)
- **Standalone mode:** returns a `ConsoleTracker` that prints to stdout

### ConsoleTracker class
Implements the same protocol as the real Tracker:
- `log_param(key: str, value: str) -> None` — prints `param: key=value`
- `log_value(key: str, value: float, step: int) -> None` — prints `[step N] key=value`
- `log_text(key: str, value: str) -> None` — prints `[text] key=value`
- `finish(results: dict[str, Any]) -> None` — prints a summary block with all results

### TrackerProtocol (for type annotations)
```python
class TrackerProtocol(Protocol):
    def log_param(self, key: str, value: str) -> None: ...
    def log_value(self, key: str, value: float, step: int) -> None: ...
    def log_text(self, key: str, value: str) -> None: ...
    def finish(self, results: dict[str, Any]) -> None: ...
```

## Env var contract

The runner (in a future task) will set `JERNERICS_TRIAL_CONFIG` before executing the trial script. For this task, just implement the reading logic — do not modify the runner.

Check `tracking/trial_environment.py` to see what tracker env vars already exist. The real tracker in job mode should be constructed the same way the current `trial()` function receives its tracker.

## Exports

Export from `jernerics/__init__.py`:
```python
from .trial_context import is_job, trial_config, trial_tracker
```

## Tests

Create `packages/jernerics/tests/unit/test_trial_context.py`:
- `is_job()` returns True/False based on env var presence
- `trial_config()` reads JSON in job mode
- `trial_config()` returns defaults in standalone mode
- `trial_config()` raises when standalone and no defaults
- `trial_config()` raises when job mode but file missing
- `trial_tracker()` returns ConsoleTracker in standalone mode
- `trial_tracker()` returns Tracker in job mode (mock env vars)
- ConsoleTracker prints to stdout for all methods
- ConsoleTracker.finish prints summary

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `trial_context.py` module created with all functions
- [ ] `ConsoleTracker` implemented with same interface as Tracker
- [ ] `TrackerProtocol` defined for type annotations
- [ ] Functions exported from `jernerics/__init__.py`
- [ ] Tests pass
- [ ] No existing code modified (purely additive)

title: Script-as-trial: migrate all symlab trial files from functions to scripts
description:
## Scope

Mechanical migration of all symlab experiment trial files from the `def trial(config, tracker)` pattern to flat scripts using the new API.

## Depends on

- `jernerics-rs5` (trial context API)
- `jernerics-7q7` (runner subprocess execution)

## What changes

Each trial file (`experiments/*/trial.py`) gets rewritten:

### Before
```python
def trial(config, tracker):
    torch.manual_seed(config["seed"])
    ...
    for step in range(config["n_steps"]):
        ...
        tracker.log_value("loss", loss.item(), step=step)
    return {"final_loss": loss.item()}
```

### After
```python
import jernerics

config = jernerics.trial_config(defaults={
    "lr": 3e-4, "n_steps": 100, ...  # pulled from each config.py
})
tracker = jernerics.trial_tracker()

torch.manual_seed(config["seed"])
...
for step in range(config["n_steps"]):
    ...
    tracker.log_value("loss", loss.item(), step=step)

tracker.finish({"final_loss": loss.item()})
```

## Per-file steps

1. Remove the `def trial(config, tracker):` wrapper, unindent the body
2. Add `import jernerics` at the top
3. Add `config = jernerics.trial_config(defaults={...})` — pull sensible defaults from the corresponding `config.py` base dict (use small n_steps like 100 for standalone)
4. Add `tracker = jernerics.trial_tracker()`
5. Replace `return {...}` with `tracker.finish({...})`
6. Ensure all `tracker.log_param()` / `tracker.log_value()` calls work unchanged (they will — same interface)

## Trial files to migrate

- `experiments/coupled/trial.py`
- `experiments/skeleton/trial.py` (symlink to coupled)
- `experiments/diagnostic/trial.py`
- `experiments/inspect/trial.py`
- `experiments/overfit/trial.py`
- `experiments/probe/trial.py`
- `experiments/scale/trial.py`

title: Container build doesn't provision external method dependencies
description:
## Problem
The container.def only runs `uv sync --no-dev --no-editable` for the main project. Methods that use external dependencies not in pyproject.toml (e.g., separate venvs, data caches) are invisible inside the container.

## Example
PySIPS originally ran as an external subprocess in a separate Python 3.12 venv with its own dependencies (pysips, bingo-nasa, smcpy). The container (Python 3.13) had no access to this venv or the SRSD data cache. This required extensive manual provisioning: venv copying, bind mounts, path overrides.

## Resolution
In this case, resolved by adding pysips/bingo-nasa/smcpy as project dependencies so they install in the container venv. But the general problem remains for any method with external dependencies.

## Suggestion
1. Document that all method dependencies must be in pyproject.toml for container builds
2. OR provide a mechanism for post-build provisioning scripts in container.def
3. OR support custom bind mounts via config (e.g., `[tool.jernerics.backends.hpc.apptainer]\nextra_binds = [...]`)

title: jernerics sync times out pulling tracking data from HPC
description:
## Problem
`jernerics sync --backend hpc` consistently times out (tested at 120s and 300s) while 'Syncing tracking data from HPC'. The SSH connection itself is fast (<1s) and the tracking data directory is small (~66M). The sync appears to hang indefinitely.

## Repro
```bash
jernerics sync --backend hpc  # hangs >300s
```

## Impact
Blocks the normal workflow of sync → run. Users must rsync code manually as a workaround.

## Workaround
Direct rsync of specific directories: `rsync -avz experiments/ jez21005@host:~/projects/symlab-overfit/experiments/`

## Environment
- Host: hpc2.storrs.hpc.uconn.edu
- pyproject.toml backend config: type=slurm, cache_dir on /scratch

title: Missing input file causes infinite retry with no fast-fail
description: When a config references a file (e.g. pool .pkl) that doesn't exist on the remote, jobs fail instantly and retry infinitely. The retry system treats each fast failure as a crash (not a permanent error), so it resubmits indefinitely with no backoff. Two problems: (1) no pre-flight validation that referenced files exist before dispatch, (2) no detection of repeated instant failures (jobs dying within seconds) to mark as permanently failed instead of retrying. In practice this means a missing pool file burns retry attempts silently and the user only discovers it by checking logs after hours of waiting.
